headline: Maye has a fractured fibula but won't need surgery

off.text: Next: Sun, Nov 29 at Chargers, 4:05 PM

storylines: Boston opens a six-game homestand after snapping a three-game skid in Detroit, but it lost its last three at TD Garden, outscored 14–4.
Jeremy Swayman (10–5–1, .908) starts, and David Pastrnak brings 28 points (10 goals, 18 assists) in 22 games.
Washington has lost four straight, outscored 23–11, and will be without defenseman Vincent Desharnais after an appendectomy.
bruins.edge: Boston on paper: 29 points from 22 games to Washington's 20 from 20, though the Capitals score 3.55 goals a game, tied for ninth in the NHL.

storylines: Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (left shoulder) are questionable as Boston tries to stop a two-game skid, with a game at Golden State on Sunday.
Sacramento is 1–14 after losing 106–104 to the Lakers on Friday, when Zach LaVine missed at the buzzer, and plays the second night of a back-to-back.
The Kings are 0–9 at home this season.
celtics.edge: Boston, clearly: it outscores opponents by 10.5 points a game, while Sacramento has been outscored by 14.0.

storylines: New England (5–5) comes off its bye at Los Angeles in a game the NFL moved from Sunday night to 4:05 p.m. on CBS.
Drake Maye has a fractured right fibula that is expected to keep him out deep into the regular season; Tommy DeVito is slated to start.
Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker are eligible to return, but A.J. Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks.
patriots.edge: New England on record (5–5 to the Chargers' 1–8), but without Maye, and its offense managed 151 yards in Munich.

celtics.headline: Tatum, White questionable at Sacramento
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum (rest) and Derrick White (left AC joint contusion) are questionable for Saturday's game against the Kings. White wasn't on the report before Wednesday's loss in Denver, where he played 35 minutes, and has played all 15 games. Boston plays at Golden State on Sunday.

celtics.headline: NBA: Tatum's late technical was the right call
celtics.summary: The league's report on the Denver game said the call was correct: "Tatum is assessed a technical foul for forcefully throwing the ball in the direction of a game official." Tatum said he should have handed the ball to the nearest official.

celtics.headline: Cenac shows flashes in Denver
celtics.summary: The 19-year-old, 6-foot-11 rookie had 6 points, 6 rebounds and a block in 17 minutes against the Nuggets, and Joe Mazzulla had him guard Jamal Murray for six possessions. "You can obviously feel a difference with his athleticism when he's out there," Mazzulla said.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla: 'We just got to be better'
celtics.summary: Joe Mazzulla didn't blame the officials for Jayson Tatum's late technical in Denver, saying it was never explained to him and that Boston can't give referees the chance to interpret it. The 105–101 loss was Boston's first back-to-back defeat of the season.

celtics.headline: A 30–13 foul gap in Denver
celtics.summary: Boston was called for 30 fouls to Denver's 13 on Wednesday, a 17-foul disparity that happened for only the 17th time in franchise history and the first since Nov. 2, 2022. The Nuggets shot 29 free throws to Boston's 12, and Paul George fouled out.

celtics.headline: Cenac pushes for Robinson's minutes
celtics.summary: MassLive's Brian Robb writes that Chris Cenac Jr. outplayed free-agent signing Mitchell Robinson off the bench in Denver. Mazzulla: "He just needs the reps to get better and better." Boston ranks 21st in the NBA on the defensive glass.

celtics.headline: Carter regaining strength after mono
celtics.summary: Devin Carter lost about 10 pounds while ill and still gets extreme fatigue for a couple of minutes at a time when running. "Just a minor setback, but definitely coming back into my body," he said. Derrick White has donated $2 million to the University of Colorado.

celtics.headline: Road trip: Kings, Warriors, then an NBA Cup game
celtics.summary: After Denver, Boston plays at Sacramento Saturday, at Golden State Sunday and at Washington in an NBA Cup game. The Celtics lead the NBA in net rating (12.1) and rank second in defensive rating (106.1).

celtics.headline: Tatum plays through a bruised hand
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum wore a wrap on his left hand against Orlando. "I bruised my hand last night," he said, adding that he wrapped it to keep the swelling down and it didn't limit him. He had no injury designation.

celtics.headline: Mazzulla on Robinson: 'bigs by committee'
celtics.summary: After Mitchell Robinson had 4 points, 5 rebounds and 5 fouls in 18 minutes against Orlando, Joe Mazzulla said: "I think he's playing a role that we need him to play. It's bigs by committee."

bruins.headline: Swayman gets the start vs. Washington
bruins.summary: Marco Sturm confirmed after Friday's practice that Jeremy Swayman will start Saturday. The lines were unchanged from the win in Detroit, with Matt Poitras on the wing with Fraser Minten and Marat Khusnutdinov, and Mikey Eyssimont among the extras.

bruins.headline: Hagens could start skating next week
bruins.summary: James Hagens, on injured reserve with a back injury, still hasn't skated, but Sturm said he "might be starting just a little bit next week to go on the ice."

bruins.headline: Bruins blocked more shots than Detroit put on goal
bruins.summary: Boston blocked 23 shots in Detroit, two more than the Red Wings' 21 shots on goal. Will Borgen led with 5 blocks, 14 of 18 skaters had at least one, and Elias Lindholm won 13 of 18 faceoffs.

bruins.headline: Swayman third in NHL.com's quarter-season goalie vote
bruins.summary: Jeremy Swayman finished third in NHL.com's staff vote with 35 points, behind Wallstedt (60) and Kochetkov (58). He is 10–5–1 with a 2.50 goals-against average, a .908 save percentage and one shutout.

bruins.headline: Lohrei and Poitras back in the lineup
bruins.summary: Mason Lohrei returned from a healthy scratch with two primary assists in Detroit, and Matt Poitras replaced Mikey Eyssimont on a line with Fraser Minten and Marat Khusnutdinov that Marco Sturm used against Detroit's top line.

bruins.headline: Power play strikes after a 4-for-31 slide
bruins.summary: Boston went 1-for-1 in Detroit, with Pavel Zacha scoring the winner off a David Pastrnak rebound. The unit had scored on four of its previous 31 chances since Oct. 27. "When it's time to shine on the power play, we strike," Marco Sturm said.

bruins.headline: Sturm: 'That's more us'
bruins.summary: Marco Sturm liked his team's attitude in the win at Detroit and said the Bruins weren't patient enough during their skid. Jeremy Swayman credited late blocked shots, and Pastrnak called it "a great bounceback game."

bruins.headline: First goal against in four straight games
bruins.summary: Boston trailed after the first period for a fourth straight game in Detroit before rallying. The Bruins' 2–1 lead in the second was their first lead since Nov. 8 against Florida.

bruins.headline: Bergeron inducted; number retired Dec. 1
bruins.summary: Patrice Bergeron was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in Toronto as one of six members of the Class of 2026. The Bruins retire his number at TD Garden on Dec. 1, with the ceremony starting at 6:10 p.m.

patriots.headline: Maye has a fractured fibula; no surgery needed
patriots.summary: Tests showed Drake Maye fractured his right fibula on the opening drive in Munich, with no additional ligament damage, and the injury won't require surgery, ESPN's Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter reported. It is expected to sideline him deep into the regular season, if he is able to return this year at all.

patriots.headline: IR limit could keep Maye on the 53
patriots.summary: The Patriots have used five of their eight IR return designations and appear to have earmarked two more for Alijah Vera-Tucker and Romeo Doubs, who are eligible to return next week. That could lead them to keep Maye on the active roster rather than move him to injured reserve.

patriots.headline: A.J. Brown expected to miss multiple weeks
patriots.summary: A.J. Brown's hamstring injury from the Lions game is expected to sideline him multiple weeks, his third missed stretch this season after a high ankle sprain and a knee flare-up. He has 11 catches for 128 yards in four games.

patriots.headline: Doubs eligible to return after the bye
patriots.summary: Patriots.com's bye-week review notes Romeo Doubs (shoulder) becomes eligible to come off injured reserve. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu are also on IR; the line has used six different combinations.

patriots.headline: Cassel's advice for DeVito
patriots.summary: Matt Cassel, who went 11–5 after replacing an injured Tom Brady in 2008, told Tommy DeVito to trust offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels: "Josh will put you in a great position to be successful."

patriots.headline: One game out of the final AFC wild card
patriots.summary: New England is 5–5 and on its bye, one game behind Cleveland for the AFC's last wild-card spot. Tommy DeVito is the starter for now after recently signing a new two-year deal.

patriots.headline: Big plays keep hurting the defense
patriots.summary: Since Week 7 the Patriots have allowed 12 pass plays of 25 or more yards, the most in the NFL. "We have to mentally be strong enough to withstand them making a play," Mike Vrabel said. New England is 5–1 against AFC teams.

patriots.headline: Chargers game flexed out of Sunday night
patriots.summary: The NFL moved Patriots at Chargers on Nov. 29 from Sunday Night Football to 4:05 p.m. on CBS; Raiders at Browns takes the 8:20 p.m. slot. New England's Dec. 10 Thursday game against Minnesota and its Dec. 21 Monday game against Kansas City stay in prime time.

patriots.headline: DeVito slated to start; Morten moves up
patriots.summary: Tommy DeVito is slated to start, with rookie Behren Morten, previously the emergency third quarterback, becoming the backup. The Patriots have a bye this week, then play at the Chargers.

redsox.headline: Gray: a Red Sox reunion 'never really came up'
redsox.summary: Sonny Gray, who signed with Minnesota, said talks with Boston "never really got close" but that "Boston was great… I loved it there, man. I truly did."

redsox.headline: Fortes to back up Rutschman
redsox.summary: Nick Fortes, acquired from Tampa Bay for 17-year-old right-hander Angel Roa, hit .258 with 6 homers and 35 RBIs in 109 games in 2026. Craig Breslow called him a "really strong defender who has a great reputation in working with a pitching staff." Connor Wong was designated for assignment to make room.

redsox.headline: Sonny Gray signs with the Twins
redsox.summary: Minnesota announced it signed Sonny Gray, reportedly to a two-year, $55 million deal. Gray went 18–5 with a 2.72 ERA for Boston in 2026 and finished fifth in AL Cy Young voting.

redsox.headline: Breslow: 'I think we have a good lineup'
redsox.summary: With Jake Bauers signed for four years and $58 million, Craig Breslow said, "I think we have a good lineup," and that it's hard to envision something else significant on the horizon. Bauers had a .389 on-base percentage in 2026, third in the majors.

redsox.headline: Two small trades clear 40-man room
redsox.summary: Boston traded left-hander Raymond Burgos to the Athletics for right-hander Kenya Huggins, opening a 40-man spot for Jake Bauers, and sent right-hander Angel Bastardo to the Royals for minor league infielder Jack Pineda.

redsox.headline: No prospects added before the Rule 5 deadline
redsox.summary: The Red Sox added no one to the 40-man roster before Tuesday's deadline, leaving Blake Wehunt, Miguel Bleis, Brooks Brannon, Johanfran Garcia, Yordanny Monegro, Hayden Mullins, Mikey Romero and Braiden Ward unprotected. Wehunt had a 3.50 ERA with 104 strikeouts in 100 1/3 innings across Double-A and Triple-A.

redsox.headline: Breslow to lead a review of the medical staff
redsox.summary: After injuries to Garrett Crochet and Roman Anthony, Craig Breslow said he will lead a thorough internal review of the team's medical staff and practices this offseason. "Without a doubt, there are things that we can do better," he said.

redsox.headline: Red Sox agree to four years with Jake Bauers
redsox.summary: Boston agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with Jake Bauers, the NLCS MVP for the champion Brewers. He hit .266 with 26 homers and 86 RBIs in 2026, mostly at first base. Because he turned down a qualifying offer, the Red Sox give up two draft picks and $1 million in international bonus pool money.

redsox.headline: Breslow promoted to president of baseball operations
redsox.summary: The Red Sox gave Craig Breslow, entering his fourth season running the club, the title of president of baseball operations, last held by Dave Dombrowski. Breslow said it doesn't change his approach.

redsox.headline: Anthony to be reassessed in two weeks
redsox.summary: Craig Breslow said Roman Anthony, who had a partially torn ligament in his right ring finger, feels good but won't swing a bat until doctors clear him. "Rest, that will be the most important part of the recovery process," Breslow said.

nba.cutNote: Top 6 make the playoffs, 7–10 the play-in

nhl.cutNote: Top 3 in each division plus 2 wild cards make the playoffs

nfl.cutNote: Top 7 make the playoffs (division winners seeded 1–4)
